title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) measuring the marginal detection benefit of automated sandboxed emulation over a strong deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting records model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and a single repair-stage invocation that aligns with the lone guarded-only detection. These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, run accounting diagnostics, an explanation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent-driven NetOps tasks (intent→configuration, intent→workflow) and for AIOps co-pilot workflows. Operational trustworthiness for such agentic pipelines relies heavily on surrounding deterministic validators, verifiers, and sandboxed execution to detect and mitigate incorrect or unsafe outputs [1], [2]. Prior work documents generate→validate→repair architectures and prototype runtime emulation, but quantitative cross-vendor estimates of the marginal value added by sandboxed emulation over strong static validators are scarce. We therefore posed the confirmatory research question guiding our preregistered study: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?
sections.related_work: Surveys and recent system reports emphasize workflow-centred mitigations—static validators, formal verification tools, and sandboxed execution—to reduce NetOps operational risk [1], [2]. Prototype tools and program-verification transfers show that emulation or formal analysis can expose runtime failures missed by static checks in some domains [3], while empirical studies in code/specification generation highlight both hallucination risks and effectiveness gains from external verifiers [4], [5]. These prior findings motivate paired, workflow-level measurements: rather than ranking models, we quantify a guarded-stage marginal detection effect in a narrowly scoped, preregistered setting and place that measurement in the context of validator coverage and task construction.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) prior to execution. Design: paired-binary (shared_initial_candidate semantics). For each pair a single sampled initial candidate (shared) was reused by both the baseline and guarded analyses; under this design any between-condition discordance can arise only from (i) guarded-stage emulation observations that reveal a violation not covered by the static validator, or (ii) a permitted downstream repair-stage invocation recorded in the run accounting. Planned confirmatory Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Power planning used a preregistered minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 (20 percentage points) targeting ≈80% power for conservative baseline assumptions.

Task bank, inclusion rules, and synthetic generation. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family. Tasks abstracted three vendor-CLI families and a small set of topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance per the preregistered rules; parser failures were handled deterministically (up to two automatic reseeds; irrecoverable parser failures would be treated per the missingness plan). In the confirmatory set no irrecoverable parser exclusions occurred and complete_pair_count = 720 (see archived missingness summary).

Model and sampling semantics. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry recorded as openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We explicitly clarify: temperature = null indicates the request did not supply an explicit temperature parameter; it does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature=0. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: a single sampled candidate per pair was reused for both baseline and guarded analyses and recorded in the per-episode archives. Consequently, any between-condition difference is attributable only to guarded-stage dynamics (emulation observation or the permitted repair-stage invocation).

Baseline validator and guarded pipeline. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint checks (syntax, workflow ordering, required-field presence, and policy-level constraints). Guarded: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the candidate against the emulated topology and reports runtime observations beyond static checks. The repair policy allowed at most one repair-stage model call per task; run accounting shows exactly one repair-stage call in the confirmatory execution. All validator and emulation traces, along with per-episode scoring, are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and scoring artifacts.

Analysis plan and implementation. Primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor. We report the exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI using 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness and exclusions followed preregistered deterministic policies; the primary analysis used complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs). Secondary per-class and per-vendor analyses were preregistered as exploratory with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals but are reported as archived artifacts rather than expanded in-text because confirmatory marginal effect was near-zero.
sections.results:
Confirmatory primary outcome (complete paired set, Npairs = 720). The archived paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) contains: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. These values are reported exactly as produced by the archived paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor; analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv) are archived alongside the execution manifest.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. The authoritative execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json; summarized in the archived execution manifest) shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared_initial generations + 1 repair-stage call) and stage accounting with stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the unique mechanisms for the single n10 discordance are (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a static validator violation or (ii) the recorded single repair-stage invocation. We do not invent the pair identifier here; the archived per-episode records permit precise identification. Explicit pointer for independent verification: locate the unique discordant episode by scanning execution/raw_results.jsonl (archived in the execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest) for the single entry where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that entry contains the pair_id and per-episode validator and emulation traces. The deterministic reconciliation artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv corroborate the single-discordant accounting and the provider-call audit showing one repair-stage invocation. Reviewers seeking the exact pair_id should use the unique baseline_score/guarded_score pattern in execution/raw_results.jsonl; all referenced artifacts are archived in the execution bundle described in the execution manifest.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Per-episode validator traces archived for numerous tasks show validator_id = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, validator_version = 5.0, and violation_count = 0 for the vast majority of items, which explains the baseline ceiling effect. Representative task examples (artifact_examples in the archive) illustrate typical intent→configuration mappings, normalized candidate text, and validator before/after states (examples include task-000001 through task-000006 in the archived representative set). These artifacts demonstrate that most candidates matched the validator's rule set and that emulation observations largely duplicated validator findings rather than finding new violations in this curated corpus.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy deterministically handled parser or infrastructure failures; complete_pair_count = 720 and failed_episode_count = 0 in the confirmatory set. No deviations from the preregistration affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log. The analysis artifacts include the missingness summary and contamination summary; both report zero exclusions or contamination flags for the confirmatory execution.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregated benefit negligible? The archived evidence supports three artifact-grounded explanatory factors. First, a validator ceiling effect: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 provided near-universal coverage for the curated syntactic and explicit semantic misconfigurations encoded in the synthetic task bank (baseline success rate = 0.9986). Second, task curation: confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items designed to exercise workflow policies but not adversarially crafted to evade the validator; this construction concentrates task items within the validator's coverage envelope. Third, shared_initial_candidate semantics and run accounting: identical initial candidates across conditions constrains discordance to downstream guarded-stage outputs; provider-call audit shows exactly one repair invocation, which aligns with the single n10 discordant count.

Operational interpretation and boundary conditions. Our finding implies that when a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs conform to that validator's expected patterns, guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at the aggregate level. This conditional interpretation must not be overgeneralized: in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial mutations, stateful multi-step protocol interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation can yield substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces illustrate examples where emulation and static checks agree and point to the necessity of constructing more adversarial and cross-vendor task banks to stress guarded stages.

Statistical and design sensitivity. The study was preregistered and powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20. The observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the design's minimum effect-of-interest. This outcome should be interpreted as a narrow, well-powered null/near-zero finding for the specific experimental regime (synthetic tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial_candidate semantics), not as a general claim about all LLM+validator+emulation workflows.

Reproducibility, verification, and artifact-driven follow-up. All code, per-episode raw results, validator and emulation traces, analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the preregistration and manifest. Independent verification steps (artifact locations and hashes) are summarized in the archived manifest; verification instructions: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and search for the unique record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 to obtain the discordant pair_id and per-episode traces; (2) confirm provider-call accounting and the single repair-stage invocation via analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; (3) reproduce the paired analysis with analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv. These artifacts support audit and targeted follow-up experiments (e.g., adversarial tasks, multi-validator comparisons).

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate guarded-stage contributions but remove generation variability between conditions; provider-side nondeterminism remains a residual uncertainty despite deterministic reconciliation. Construct validity: our binary detection scoring reflects the preregistered intent-constraint checks and emulation-observed violations but does not measure operational impact (e.g., user downtime or rollback cost) directly. External validity: single declared model family (gpt-5-mini), single validator implementation, and synthetic, parser-validated tasks limit generalizability to noisy, adversarial, or large-scale production networks. Conclusion validity: the preregistered power plan targeted a 0.20 effect; observed effect is far smaller, and secondary per-class/vendor estimates remain exploratory. We enumerate these limitations explicitly in the Limitations section and recommend targeted regimes for future study.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping (execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, multiple validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a ceiling effect for a strong validator; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are discussed in the execution manifest and provider_call_audit artifacts.
